newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Tajik rebels release five hostages -- Tass.
newsitem.headline: Tajik rebels release five hostages -- Tass.

text.p: Tajik rebels holding 11 Russian and Western hostages in their remote mountain stronghold have released five of their captives, Itar-Tass news agency said on Sunday.
The announcement came shortly after Tajik President Imomali Rakhmonov agreed to hold direct talks with rebel leader Bakhrom Sadirov early on Monday near the rebels' base.

The five hostages freed include a Swiss military observer working with the United Nations, two Russian television reporters, a Tajik interpreter and an employee of the U.N. refugee agency, Tass said, quoting rebel sources.
The freed hostages were expected to arrive shortly at the village of Obigarm at the foot of the rebels' mountain base, it addded.

Two other U.N. military observers -- a Swiss and a Ukrainian -- several more U.N. officials and the Tajik Security Minister Saidamir Zukhorov are still being held, even though the Tajik government has met all demands for their release.

In the Tajik capital Dushanbe presidential spokesman Zafar Saidov earlier told Reuters that Rakhmonov would travel to Obigarm to begin direct talks with the rebels at 9 a.m. (0400 GMT) on Monday. Sadirov has said none of the hostages will be harmed.
